title: Patch: a match in a background tab plays no crowd murmurs, as its sound effects and voices already stay quiet
thread:
**Issue #4512 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4512: Patch: a match in a background tab plays no crowd murmurs, as its sound effects and voices already stay quiet
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When a player switches to another tab in the middle of a match, the game already silences its sound effects and voice lines. The crowd's quiet background murmurs carry on, though: a short burst of chatter every 6 to 15 seconds from a tab the player is not looking at, until the match ends or they come back. Once this is built, a match in a background tab makes no crowd noise, and the murmurs resume when the player returns.

## Why

- **Effects and voices are gated on a hidden page.** The engine's gate, `accepting()` (`apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts:534-540`), drops anything asked for while the page is hidden (`visibility() === 'hidden'`). Hiding the page only silences the voice (`onLifecycle`, `engine.ts:468-474`); the audio context is never suspended, and desktop browsers keep a hidden tab's audio context running.
- **The crowd skips that gate.**
  - Its `live()` (`apps/web/src/audio/crowd.ts:139-143`) checks only that the context is `running`.
  - The murmur loop (`crowd.ts:147-160`) fires every `CROWD_FEEL.patronMinMs` to `patronMaxMs` (6,000 to 15,000 ms, `game/damageFeel.ts:32-35`), from `crowd.start()` (`audio/useGameAudio.ts:139-148`) until the board leaves or the game ends.
  - Each murmur is a 0.34 s band-passed noise burst (`crowd.ts:60-84`) on the crowd bus. That bus defaults to 0.5 (`audio/settings.ts:17`), and only Mute silences it (`audio/mix.ts:75,94`).
- **The crowd's own test assumes a hidden page means a stopped context:** 'the page hides and the OS stops the context' (`crowd.test.ts:142-170`). That holds when a phone puts the app away, not for a desktop browser tab.
- **The Audio settings promise quiet.** The hint reads 'Sound effects and voices stay quiet either way' (`audio/AudioControls.tsx:53`), and the music fades while the page is hidden too (`audio/music.ts:98`). SPEC §10.11 says nothing about the crowd while the page is hidden.

## Proposal

- Drop a murmur or a crowd reaction that comes due while the page is hidden, exactly as one due on a suspended context is dropped today. Nothing is saved up to burst out on return, and the murmur loop keeps its rhythm.
- The simplest seam: the engine's `crowdOutput()` (`engine.ts:1186`) returns null while `visibility()` says hidden, and `live()` already treats null as no output. If the builder prefers the crowd to read visibility itself, a visibility port on `CrowdDirectorOptions` works too.
- The crowd follows the effects' rule, quiet while hidden whatever the setting says, not the music's 'Keep playing music when this tab is in the background', which stays music-only. A window that is visible but not focused keeps its crowd, as it keeps its effects.
- Add a ruling numbered in the issue's block: the crowd is quiet while the page is hidden, as the effects and voices are. Its §11 paragraph goes in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`, and its test is named after it.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts` (or `apps/web/src/audio/crowd.ts`) and `apps/web/src/audio/crowd.test.ts`
- `spec/rulings/R<next>.md` in the issue's block and `spec/pending/<issue>.md` (SPEC §10.11)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the context `running` and the page hidden, a murmur and a crowd reaction that come due (a GIGA hit's roar) play nothing on the crowd bus. The test sets the engine's `visibility` option, as `engine.test.ts`'s rig does.
- [ ] The murmur loop stays scheduled while hidden, and on return only the next murmur due plays; nothing held back plays as a burst.
- [ ] The existing crowd tests pass unchanged: the suspended and interrupted context, the rebuilt context, and #352's murmurs.
- [ ] The new ruling note lists its test in `proven_in`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/crowd.test.ts src/audio/engine.test.ts` passes.

## Size and risks

Small: one or two source lines in one file, plus a test and a ruling note. The one risk is a crowd that fails to come back once the page shows again. The return test covers that, and since the context is never touched, nothing has to be resumed.

---

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45077442139)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

A match in a hidden tab plays no crowd sound: with the context `running` and the page hidden, a murmur or reaction that comes due is dropped exactly like one due on a suspended context, the murmur loop keeps its rhythm, and on return only the next murmur due plays with nothing bursting out. The change is one gate line in the engine, one new test named after a new ruling, and the ruling note plus its pending §11 paragraph.

## Files to touch

| File | New/change | What changes |
|------|------------|--------------|
| `apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts` | change | `crowdOutput()` (line 1186): return null while `visibility()` is `"hidden"`, with an `R4512000` comment |
| `apps/web/src/audio/crowd.test.ts` | change | New `it("R4512000 …")` in the background `describe` (lines 101–192), reusing its `due`/`heard` helpers |
| `spec/rulings/R4512000.md` | new | Ruling note, first free number in issue #4512's block |
| `spec/pending/4512.md` | new | The §11 paragraph for this issue's branch |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`; no `crates/` file; no other spec note, and leave `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md` and `spec/CARDS.md` alone (the daily fold writes them). Governing spec: `§10.11` (Autoplay, Settings), `R631`, `R669`.

## Steps

1. In `apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts`, change `crowdOutput` (line 1186) so it returns null while the page is hidden:
   `crowdOutput: () => (ctx === null || buses === null || disposed || visibility() === "hidden" ? null : { context: ctx, crowd: buses.crowd }),`
   Add a one-line comment above it citing the ruling, e.g. `// R4512000: the crowd bus is closed while the page is hidden, as effects and voices are.` No other engine code changes: `live()` in `apps/web/src/audio/crowd.ts` (lines 140–143) already treats a null output as no output, so murmurs (lines 152–162) and reactions (lines 176–195) due while hidden are dropped, and `schedulePatron` still reschedules, keeping the rhythm. Copy the `accepting()` gate pattern at lines 534–540.
2. In `apps/web/src/audio/crowd.test.ts`, add `it("R4512000 the crowd stays quiet while the page is hidden and murmurs again on return", …)` inside the existing `describe("background: … (issue #2034)")`, reusing its `due`, `heard` and `crowdBusOf` helpers. Build its engine with an explicit visibility port as `engine.test.ts`'s rig does: `let visibility: DocumentVisibilityState = "visible";` and `createAudioEngine({ createContext: factory.create, lifecycle: null, speech: null, visibility: () => visibility })`. Get the crowd bus via `crowdBusOf` while still visible (it throws on a null output).
3. In the new test: `crowd.start()`; `crowd.observeDamage(25)` while visible (a GIGA hit, so its roar is pending behind `CROWD_FEEL.reactionDebounceMs`); set `visibility = "hidden"`; fire `due(tasks)`; assert `heard(audio, bus)` is empty (murmur and roar dropped). Then assert a `crowd.observeDamage(25)` asked for while hidden schedules nothing (`tasks` length unchanged). Assert the murmur loop is still scheduled: exactly one live task with `ms >= CROWD_FEEL.patronMinMs` remains, as the suspended-context test does at line 159.
4. Still in the test: set `visibility = "visible"`; fire `due(tasks)`; assert `heard(audio, bus)` has length 1 (only the next murmur due, no burst). End with `expect(audio.violations).toEqual([])`.
5. Write `spec/rulings/R4512000.md` in the format of `spec/rulings/R0702.md`: front matter `id: R4512000`, a title naming the question (mention `issue #4512`), `cards: "§10.11, R631, R669, issue #4512"`, `proven_in: [apps/web/src/audio/crowd.test.ts]`. Body: the crowd is quiet while the page is hidden whatever the audio settings say, following the effects' rule rather than the music's "Keep playing music when this tab is in the background" setting (`§10.11`, `R631`); a visible-but-unfocused window keeps its crowd, as it keeps its effects; link each ruling/section as `[[R631]]`, `[[R669]]`, `[[§10.11]]`. Record the rejected alternative: gating on the music background setting.
6. Write `spec/pending/4512.md` holding the one §11 paragraph in the style of `spec/pending/4424.md`: `**[[R4512000]] <title> (issue #4512, 2026-11-22)**: <one-paragraph summary>`.
7. Do not edit `spec/10-engine-guide.md` §10.11 body, `crowd.ts`, `useGameAudio.ts`, settings or mix files: the issue scopes the spec change to the ruling note plus pending paragraph, and no source change beyond the gate line is needed.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/audio/crowd.test.ts`, `it("R4512000 the crowd stays quiet while the page is hidden and murmurs again on return")`: asserts hidden-due murmur and GIGA roar play nothing, hidden `observeDamage` schedules nothing, the loop stays scheduled (one live patron task), and on return exactly one murmur plays with no burst and no audio violations.
- Existing `apps/web/src/audio/crowd.test.ts` tests pass unchanged (#352 murmurs, suspended/interrupted drop, rebuilt context), proving no regression.
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/crowd.test.ts src/audio/engine.test.ts`, then `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] With context `running` and page hidden, a due murmur and a due GIGA roar play nothing on the crowd bus.
- [ ] The murmur loop stays scheduled while hidden; on return only the next murmur due plays.
- [ ] Existing crowd tests pass unchanged, and the engine test file still passes.
- [ ] The ruling note lists its test in `proven_in`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` is clean (no other checks needed for this scope).

## Risks

- A crowd that never comes back: avoided because the context is never touched — only the output gate closes, so return needs no resume; the return assertion covers it.
- `document.visibilityState` defaulting to something other than `"visible"` in jsdom would break existing crowd tests after the gate: the existing tests use the default port, so if they still pass the default is not `"hidden"`; the new test uses an explicit port either way.
- No §10.11 body edit is a deliberate scoping choice per the issue's Where-it-lands; if the reviewer wants the Autoplay bullet extended, that is a one-sentence follow-up.

## Open questions

None.
```
